score.notes: A confident, symmetrical Mughal-inflected facade with a clear base→body→crown reading: white plinth with inset studs, a lapis-blue body of three recessed bays, and a stepped gold onion-dome crown with a slender finial, flanked by banded corner minarets. Proportion is deliberate and coherent — the side-center-side bay rhythm and framing towers are well judged — but it stops short of inevitable: the crowning dome reads slightly undersized against the broad, faintly squat body, and the corner finials are stubby, so a designer could still tune the massing. Color is disciplined and harmonious — gold dominant, lapis supporting, quartz-white structure, crimson notes — genuinely colorful and on-brief, though the gold runs hot enough to flatten hierarchy in places, keeping it short of an identity-defining scheme. Detail is the weakest axis: the relief gestures (recessed bays, gold string-courses, pilaster banding, stepped dome) are real, but the three large blue panels are mostly flat fields carrying only sparse applied ornament — small crimson plus-motifs and a thin diamond drop — so close inspection finds empty wall rather than layered articulation. Fidelity is strong: the dome, twin minarets, and central gold ogee-arch portal make it unmistakably a temple with genuine presence and a legible entrance, though the central niche reads more as a blind decorative arch than a deep doorway, so it lands as a characterful temple rather than an iconic, namable landmark. Holistically a strong, photogenic build held back from exceptional by flat bay fields and a crown that wants a touch more height and authority.
